name: _to_sparse_csc
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI; the other registered overloads and their keyword-only/aliasing/mutation behavior remain owned by the original Gems pytest): aten::_to_sparse_csc(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. Registered schemas (verbatim): "aten::_to_sparse_csc(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor"; "aten::_to_sparse_csc.out(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)". The `.out` overload is keyword-only on `out`, mutates `out` and returns it aliased, and is exercised by the pytest out= workloads; that conditional, overload-dependent behavior is described here rather than modeled in this single-overload definition. Semantics: convert a dense tensor with rank >= 2 into a sparse CSC tensor, dropping only exact zeros (no rounding, so positive cases are compared exactly). `dense_dim` selects the number of trailing payload axes that stay dense; the two axes before them become the sparse matrix (rows x cols) and the remaining leading axes become batch axes, so the result carries per-slice ccol_indices/row_indices and int32 index buffers. dense_dim defaults to None (and may be omitted entirely, which is distinct from an explicit None, though both select zero dense payload axes), must lie in [0, rank - 2], is cast to Optional[int] (a float is rejected), and values outside the window or rank-deficient inputs raise RuntimeError, while omitting dense_dim on a rank < 2 input raises IndexError. Zero-sized extents, non-contiguous/storage-offset/transposed views, NaN/Inf inputs, batched slices with equal nnz but distinct zero patterns, and the input being left unmutated are all part of the contract. Keyword handling, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation remain defined by the original Gems pytest; do not narrow that coverage to this representative signature.
